nes.name: NES / Famicom
nes.resolution_note: 256x240 rendered; NTSC TVs show ~256x224 (8 lines cropped top/bottom)
nes.palette_note: 64 entries in PPU index order $00-$3F, 'classic' FCEUX/Nestopia-style 2C02 NTSC palette (the same 55-value set Lospec publishes as 'NES'). $0D/$0E/$0F/$1D-$1F/$2E/$2F/$3E/$3F are blacks ($0D is 'blacker than black', avoid) -> 54 distinct usable colors. No single canonical 2C02 RGB set exists; NesDev publishes signal-derived alternatives.
nes.onscreen_note: 4 BG palettes x 3 colors + 1 shared backdrop = 13 BG colors, plus 4 sprite palettes x 3 = 12 -> 25 on screen; each 16x16 px BG block limited to one 4-color palette (attribute table)
nes.dither_note: Checkerboard/stipple dithering inside a tile using the 3 palette colors + backdrop; color count limited per 16x16 attribute block (attribute clash), so artists rely on palette choice more than dither. Composite NTSC blending also blurs adjacent columns.

gameboy_dmg.name: Game Boy (DMG) - mono green
gameboy_dmg.shades_note: Classic widely used DMG set (darkest->lightest). Alternates: Wikipedia 'List of video game console palettes' 294139/39594A/5A7942/7B8210; BGB emulator 081820/346856/88C070/E0F8D0; SameBoy DMG 081810/396139/84A563/C6DE8C.
gameboy_dmg.dither_note: 2-bit greenscale: checkerboard/stipple dithering between the 4 shades is common (e.g. faux mid-tones, transparency via alternating-frame flicker exploiting LCD ghosting). BGP/OBP0/OBP1 remap the 4 shades per layer.

gameboy_pocket.name: Game Boy Pocket (MGB) - mono gray
gameboy_pocket.shades_note: Wikipedia 'List of video game console palettes' Pocket set (darkest->lightest). Alternates: SameBoy MGB (olive) 07100E/3A4C3A/818D66/C2CE93; pure 2-bit grayscale 000000/555555/AAAAAA/FFFFFF (Lospec '2-bit grayscale' uses 000000/676767/B6B6B6/FFFFFF); Lospec 'PocketGB' (photographed) 4E3F2A/605444/887B6A/AEA691.
gameboy_pocket.dither_note: Same as DMG: 2-bit checkerboard/stipple dithering; FSTN LCD shows true gray so dithers read cleaner than on the DMG.

gameboy_light.name: Game Boy Light (MGB-101) - mono warm/backlit
gameboy_light.shades_note: Wikipedia 'List of video game console palettes' Game Boy Light (backlit) set: the EL backlight gives a teal/blue-green glow (Bulbapedia: 'light cyan, cyan, dark cyan, black'). Alternate: SameBoy GB_PALETTE_GBL 0A1C15/357862/56B495/7FE2C3. With backlight off it looks like the Pocket gray set.

virtual_boy.name: Virtual Boy - mono red
virtual_boy.shades_note: Black + 3 red LED intensities (2-bit). Lospec 'Virtual Boy' (sampled from screenshots): 000000/550000/A40000/EF0000. Alternate linear set used by Mednafen/most emulators: 000000/550000/AA0000/FF0000. Hardware brightness registers (BRTA/BRTB/BRTC) are programmable so the 3 red levels vary per game.
virtual_boy.dither_note: 2-bit red: checkerboard dithering between brightness levels; per-column LED scanning means fine vertical patterns are common. Games also use 'gradient' effects via per-frame brightness changes.

gameboy_color.name: Game Boy Color (classic 16)
gameboy_color.onscreen_note: 8 BG palettes x 4 + 8 OBJ palettes x 3 = 56 without tricks (Wikipedia). DMG games in compatibility mode: 4 BG + 2x3 OBJ = up to 10.

default_dmg_compat_palette.note: 'Dark green' default used for unrecognized mono cartridges (also Right+A). Decoded from the CGB boot ROM palette table (SameBoy cgb_boot.asm), 5-bit->8-bit round(v*255/31).

gameboy_color.suggested_16_note: 'Classic 16' is not a hardware term; this is a derived 16-color union of the default + most-used built-in DMG-compat palettes (BG colors) - use it if the plugin means a 16-entry look, otherwise quantize to 5-5-5 with 56 colors.
gameboy_color.dither_note: Little dithering needed: 4 colors per 8x8 tile palette (attribute per tile), 15-bit RGB. Artists blend by picking per-tile palettes; occasional checkerboard inside tiles. LCD has muted saturation - emulators apply 'color correction'.

c64.name: Commodore 64
c64.resolution_note: Hires 320x200 (2 colors per 8x8 cell); Multicolor 160x200 (double-wide px, 4 colors per 4x8 cell). Overscan area 403x284 PAL not drawable.
c64.palette_note: Chosen: Pepto (2001, PAL) palette in VIC-II index order 0-15 - the most widely cited set and the classic VICE default. Alternate 'Colodore' (Pepto 2015 recalculation, now VICE/Lospec default): 000000 FFFFFF 813338 75CEC8 8E3C97 56AC4D 2E2C9B EDF171 8E5029 553800 C46C71 4A4A4A 7B7B7B A9FF9F 706DEB B2B2B2.
c64.dither_note: Attribute clash: hires = 2 colors per 8x8 cell; multicolor = 3 free + 1 global background per 4x8 cell of 2:1 wide pixels. Typical dithering is horizontal/vertical stipple (checkerboard reads badly with 2:1 pixels) and 'PAL blending' of adjacent same-luma colors; Koala/IFLI use interlace/flicker to mix colors.

atari_2600.name: Atari 2600
atari_2600.resolution_note: 160 color clocks wide (playfield 40 blocks of 4 px), ~192 visible NTSC lines (up to 262 total); pixel aspect ~1.6:1
atari_2600.palette_structure: NTSC: 16 hues x 8 luminances = 128 colors (byte = hhhhllll, luma in bits 1-3); PAL: 104 usable (13 hues x 8); SECAM: 8. Too many to list (>64): use a TIA NTSC palette table (Stella emulator default, or Lospec 'Atari 2600').
atari_2600.onscreen_note: Only 4 color registers (background, playfield/ball, player0/missile0, player1/missile1) per scanline, but all can be rewritten every scanline ('racing the beam'), so whole palette can appear per frame.
atari_2600.dither_note: No pixel dithering in the usual sense: color changes per scanline (raster bars/gradients) are the idiom; horizontal stripes and 'venetian blind' line alternation; flicker (alternate frames) to multiplex sprites and mix colors.
atari_2600.palette_note: APPROXIMATION: TIA 16 hues x 4 of 8 lumas synthesised in HLS (no canonical table); replace with a Stella NTSC table when wanted

zx_spectrum.name: ZX Spectrum
zx_spectrum.palette_note: Wikipedia 'ZX Spectrum' / 8-bit list values (basic level 0xD7=215, bright 0xFF); 15 distinct colors since basic black = bright black. Variants: Lospec uses D8 (85% voltage), some emulators CD (205).
zx_spectrum.dither_note: Attribute clash: each 8x8 cell has 1 INK + 1 PAPER from the same BRIGHT level (BRIGHT/FLASH per cell). Dithering = checkerboard/stipple between ink and paper within a cell to fake a third tone; artists align art to the 8x8 attribute grid.

pico8.name: PICO-8
pico8.palette_note: Official 16 (indices 0-15). A second 'secret' set (128-143) exists: 291814 111D35 422136 125359 742F29 49333B A28879 F3EF7D BE1250 FF6C24 A8E72E 00B543 065AB5 754665 FF6E59 FF9D81.
pico8.dither_note: Free per-pixel color (no attributes), so classic checkerboard and 'fillp' 4x4 fill patterns between two palette colors are the norm; palette swaps (pal()) for shading.

ega16.name: IBM PC EGA (16)
ega16.resolution_note: 320x200 16-color (mode 0Dh) most common for games; also 640x200 and 640x350 16-color
ega16.palette_note: Default 16 (identical to CGA RGBI colors); EGA can remap each of the 16 to any of 64 (2 bits per channel, levels 00/55/AA/FF) in 350-line modes.
ega16.dither_note: Free per-pixel, 16 colors: heavy checkerboard/ordered dithering to fake more shades (Sierra/LucasArts EGA look); artists also exploit the 64-color re-palette on 640x350.

master_system.name: Sega Master System
master_system.onscreen_note: 2 palettes of 16 (BG, sprites); BG tiles may use either; 31 + backdrop
master_system.palette_note: All 64 colors listed in CRAM byte order (--BBGGRR), levels 00/55/AA/FF.
master_system.dither_note: Coarse 2-bit-per-channel steps, so checkerboard and vertical-line dither between neighbouring levels are common; composite output blends them. 8x8 tile picks one of 2 palettes.

snes.name: SNES / Super Famicom (subset)
snes.onscreen_note: 256-entry CGRAM: 8 BG palettes x 16 (mode 1) + 8 sprite palettes x 16; mode 7 uses all 256; direct-color 2048
snes.dither_note: Rarely needed - 15-bit RGB with 16 colors per tile; ordered/checkerboard dither used mainly in mode-7 ground textures and pseudo-transparency (alternating pixel columns blend on composite); color math (half-add) handles transparency.

amiga_ocs.name: Amiga OCS/ECS
amiga_ocs.resolution_note: PAL lo-res 320x256 (NTSC 320x200); hi-res 640x256/512; interlace doubles vertical
amiga_ocs.onscreen_note: 32 in lo-res (5 bitplanes); 64 in Extra-Half-Brite; 4096 in HAM6; Copper can change palette per scanline
amiga_ocs.dither_note: Ordered (Bayer) dithering and hand checkerboards very common in Amiga art/demos; 'copper gradients' for skies; HAM/EHB tricks; 16-color hi-res games often dither heavily.

apple_ii.name: Apple II (6-color hi-res)
apple_ii.resolution_note: 280x192 monochrome bitmap; effective color resolution 140x192 (color = pair of pixels); lo-res 40x48 16 colors
apple_ii.palette_note: Wikipedia 'Apple II graphics' YIQ-derived sRGB (purple=lo-res 3, green=12, orange=9, blue=6). Common emulator alternate (AppleWin-style): purple FF44FD, green 14F53C, orange FF6A3C, blue 14CFFD.
apple_ii.dither_note: NTSC artifact color: hue depends on pixel column parity (even=purple/blue, odd=green/orange) and the per-byte high bit (palette shift), so every 7-pixel byte is either the purple/green or blue/orange pair; adjacent lit pixels turn white. Dithering = alternating columns to mix hues; 'color fringing' on edges.

apple_iigs.name: Apple IIgs
apple_iigs.onscreen_note: 16 colors per scanline from 16 stored palettes -> up to 256 on screen; 3200-color mode via per-line palette loading
apple_iigs.dither_note: 640 mode uses hardware 'fill/dither' (alternating even/odd pixel palettes blend to fake 16 colors); 320 mode uses ordered dither and per-scanline palette swaps.

game_gear.name: Sega Game Gear
game_gear.dither_note: Same VDP as Master System; 12-bit color reduces need for dither, but 16 colors per tile group leads to checkerboard shading; the blurry LCD smears fine dithers into gradients.

msx.name: MSX (MSX1 / TMS9918, 16)
msx.palette_note: Wikipedia 'List of 8-bit computer hardware graphics' TMS9918 (MSX) set, index 0 = transparent (shown as black). openMSX default is nearly identical (3EB849/74D07D/5955E0/...). MSX2 has 3-3-3 (512) with 16 on screen.
msx.dither_note: Screen 2: 2 colors per 8x1 pixel line segment (per byte) - 'attribute clash' per row of 8, finer than Spectrum. Dithering: horizontal stipple within an 8x1 run and vertical alternation between rows.

amstrad_cpc.name: Amstrad CPC
amstrad_cpc.resolution_note: Mode 0: 160x200 16 colors (2:1 wide px) - typical for games; Mode 1: 320x200 4 colors; Mode 2: 640x200 2 colors
amstrad_cpc.palette_note: 27 colors = 3 levels per channel (0/0x80/0xFF), listed in firmware INK number order 0-26. Lospec 'Amstrad CPC' uses near-identical values (e.g. 040404, 7F/80).
amstrad_cpc.dither_note: No attribute clash (per-pixel color from the chosen 16 of 27). Mode 0 art uses horizontal stipple / checkerboard between the wide pixels; Mode 1 (4 colors) relies on heavy checkerboard dithering.

ti99.name: TI-99/4A (TMS9918A, 16)
ti99.palette_note: TI datasheet-derived TMS9918A set used by MAME/Classic99 and long-standing Wikipedia TMS9918 table. Current Wikipedia 'TMS9918' gamma-corrected alternate: 000000 0AAD1E 34C84C 2B2DE3 514BFB BD2925 1EE2EF FB2C2B FF5F4C BDA22B D7B454 0A8C18 AF329A B2B2B2 FFFFFF.
ti99.dither_note: Same VDP as MSX1: Graphics II mode = 2 colors per 8x1 segment; 'bitmap' art dithers horizontally within a byte and alternates rows; 4-color 'multicolor' mode 64x48 blocks.

pc98.name: NEC PC-9801 / PC-98
pc98.onscreen_note: 16 from 4096 (VM/VX and later); early models 8 digital RGB; PC-9821 adds 256 from 16.7M
pc98.default_palette_note: Digital 8-color set (index bits G-R-B): 000000 0000FF FF0000 FF00FF 00FF00 00FFFF FFFF00 FFFFFF; analog boot default = these at reduced level (0-7) + full level (8-15).
pc98.dither_note: The defining PC-98 look: 640x400 at 16 colors forces intensive ordered/checkerboard dithering ('tile dithering', 2x2/4x4 patterns) for skin and gradients in visual novels; 1:1.2 non-square pixels on early CRTs.

cga.name: IBM PC CGA
cga.palette_note: Full 16-color RGBI list; 320x200 games see only 4 (background selectable from 16). Brown (AA5500) is the RGBI monitor's special case (would be AAAA00 = dark yellow on a naive RGBI decode).
cga.dither_note: Cyan/magenta/white (palette 1) checkerboards everywhere; composite CGA artifact colors (16 shades at 160x200) from 4-pixel patterns; ordered dither to fake extra colors.

vga16.name: IBM PC VGA (16)
vga16.resolution_note: 16-color VGA modes: 640x480 (12h) and 640x350; most 16-color VGA-era games actually ran 320x200 (EGA-style, mode 0Dh/1 pixel aspect 1.2:1). Mode 13h 320x200 = 256 colors.
vga16.palette_note: Default 16 = CGA/EGA RGBI colors; VGA DAC is 6 bits per channel (262,144) so each entry is re-programmable.
vga16.dither_note: Ordered/checkerboard dithering as on EGA; 640x480 16-color Windows-era art uses fine 2x2 patterns.

tandy_pcjr.name: Tandy 1000 / PCjr (TGA 16)
tandy_pcjr.palette_note: Same 16 RGBI colors as CGA, all usable at once.
tandy_pcjr.dither_note: 16 free colors per pixel: Sierra 'Tandy' versions used checkerboard dithering between RGBI colors for skin tones and gradients.

hercules.name: Hercules (amber mono)
hercules.shades_note: 1-bit hardware: black + phosphor color. Amber P3 phosphor commonly approximated FFB000 (also FFBF00 'amber', FFAA00); intermediate shades are only for CRT glow/bloom emulation, not hardware. Green P1 alternative ~33FF33.
hercules.dither_note: Pure 1-bit: all tone comes from ordered (Bayer) or error-diffusion dithering of black/amber pixels; very fine 720x348 grid, non-square pixels (~1.55:1 aspect correction).

macintosh_1bit.name: Macintosh 1-bit (B/W)
macintosh_1bit.shades_note: Hardware is pure 1-bit black/white; intermediate shades only if the shader wants a 4-level ramp.
macintosh_1bit.dither_note: The canonical dither platform: Floyd-Steinberg / Atkinson (Bill Atkinson's MacPaint) error diffusion and 8x8 ordered patterns at 72 dpi square pixels.

pc88.name: NEC PC-8801 (PC-88, 8)
pc88.resolution_note: 640x200 8 colors (V1); 640x400 2 colors; SR and later: 8 of 512 (3-3-3)
pc88.palette_note: Digital RGB 8 colors (index bit order G-R-B on the hardware). PC-8801mkII SR+ can remap the 8 to any of 512 (3-3-3).
pc88.dither_note: 8 saturated colors at 640x200 (2:1 tall pixels): PC-88 art is famous for dense 'tile' / checkerboard dithering to fake mid-tones and skin.

x68000.name: Sharp X68000
x68000.bits_note: 16-bit palette entry GGGGGRRRRRBBBBBI: 5-5-5 RGB + 1 shared intensity/luminance LSB
x68000.onscreen_note: 256-color graphics layer (or 65536 direct at 512x512); sprites/BG use 16 palettes x 16 from the 65536
x68000.dither_note: Arcade-style: little dithering; 16-color sprite palettes, checkerboard used for pseudo-transparency and shadows; 256-color layer for backgrounds.

atari_st.name: Atari ST
atari_st.resolution_note: Low res 320x200 16 colors; medium 640x200 4; high 640x400 mono
atari_st.onscreen_note: STE: 4-4-4 (4096); raster tricks (Spectrum 512) get more per line
atari_st.dither_note: 16 colors at 320x200 -> ordered dithering and checkerboards everywhere (Degas/NeoChrome era); no hardware assist, composite/RF blur hides it.

bbc_micro.name: BBC Micro (Mode 2, 8)
bbc_micro.resolution_note: MODE 2: 160x256, 16 logical colours (8 + 8 flashing) with 2:1 wide pixels; MODE 1 320x256 4 colours; MODE 5 160x256 4
bbc_micro.palette_note: 8 saturated TTL RGB colours (BBC order 0-7: black, red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, white) plus flashing variants 8-15.
bbc_micro.dither_note: Per-pixel colour (no attribute clash) but wide pixels and only 8 hues: stipple/checkerboard dithering between primaries to fake browns, oranges, greys.

pc_engine.name: PC Engine / TurboGrafx-16
pc_engine.resolution_note: 256-wide low-res is most common; vertical 224 (visible) to 239/240; 336 and 512 wide also supported
pc_engine.onscreen_note: 16 BG palettes x 16 + 16 sprite palettes x 16 = 512 entries, 482 unique on screen
pc_engine.dither_note: Rarely dithers; 16-color palettes per tile give rich art. Composite output of 256-wide modes blends any checkerboards used for shadows/transparency.

mega_drive.name: Sega Mega Drive / Genesis
mega_drive.onscreen_note: 4 palettes x 16 (index 0 transparent) = 61 unique + backdrop; Shadow/Highlight mode ~1536 tones
mega_drive.dither_note: Signature look: vertical-line and checkerboard dithering between two palette colours, relied on composite/RF blur to blend into new colours and pseudo-transparency (water in Sonic); 3-3-3 steps make ramps coarse.
